bullets.title: TSM: Record Q2 beat, FY26 guide to >40% growth, capex to $60-64B + $100B Arizona expansion
bullets.body: TSMC delivered Q2 EPS of $4.31 (+14% vs $3.77 consensus) on $40.2B revenue; gross margin 67.7% beat the 65.5-67.5% guidance range. FY26 revenue guide raised to 'slightly above' 40% YoY (vs prior 'above 30%'), capex raised to $60-64B, and CEO Wei announced an additional $100B Arizona investment (four new N2 fabs + advanced packaging). Q3 guide of $44.6-45.8B revenue and 65-67% GM both beat consensus. JPM flagged gross margin miss vs their 69.5% expectation as the key negative; Jefferies notes N2 ramp dilution driving the GM step-down to ~66% in Q3 but expects a return to high-60s as N3 crosses corporate average in 2H26. Stock traded -4.5% pre-market, driving broad semi selloff.

bullets.title: Semi complex broad selloff on TSM margin miss—WDC -7.8%, MU -4.7%, ALAB/CRDO/MRVL all -4%+
bullets.body: Pre-market semiconductor complex was sharply lower post-TSM results: WDC -7.8%, SNDK -7.2%, STX -6.4%, MU -4.7%, ALAB -4.5%, CRDO -4.3%, MRVL -4.2%, CIEN -4.1%, COHR -5.0%, VRT -3.5%, AVGO -2.1%, AMD -3.4%, INTC -3.1%. GS desk notes demand for hyperscalers vs. supply in semis; GOOGL/MSFT/META/ORCL outperforming as flight-to-quality trade. JPM characterizes Korean levered ETF tightening as creating near-term mechanical downside for the complex.

bullets.title: NVDA: Japan buys 27,500 Rubin chips (~$1.4B) for national physical AI; new Jetson Thor T3000/T2000 modules launched
bullets.body: Japan's government-backed Noetra Corp will deploy 13,750 Vera CPUs and 27,500 Rubin GPUs—world's first national physical AI infrastructure. Separately, NVDA launched Jetson Thor T3000 and T2000 for mainstream robotics/edge AI (50% size reduction vs. prior), and announced expanded partnerships with Toyota, Kawasaki, Mitsubishi Heavy, and Japanese banks (Mizuho, MUFG) deploying Nemotron models. Oppenheimer reiterates NVDA as top pick with Blackwell+Rubin cumulative revenues >$1T 2025-27E.

bullets.title: NFLX: Heading into earnings with short bias; bears flag engagement plateau and FX guide risk
bullets.body: Jefferies notes NFLX is headed into Q2 earnings with a short bias—bears position for flat engagement, rising churn, and potential constant-currency revenue guide cuts, with multiple compression vs. legacy media still needed. Management comment on ad-supported tier trajectory and subscriber growth will be key. NFLX reports after close tonight.

bullets.title: AMZN: KeyBanc raises PT to $335; AWS +33% Q2 expected, $485B backlog, Trainium3 ramp
bullets.body: KeyBanc raises AMZN PT to $335 (25.5x 2028E P/E) and maintains Overweight. AWS expected to grow +33% Y/Y in 2Q26 vs. Street +31%; AWS backlog estimated at ~$485B partly anchored by $100B Anthropic agreement. 2027E/2028E capex forecast at $331B/$356B vs. Street's $235B/$241B. Citi separately raised AWS projections to +32.5% Q2/+40% for 2027, alongside materially higher CapEx forecasts driving negative FCF in 2027-28E.

bullets.title: GOOGL/META/MSFT: Citi raises CapEx materially; negative FCF projected 2027-28E; desk sees flight-to-quality
bullets.body: Citi raised 2027E CapEx for GOOGL (+21% to $308B including ~$62B TPU sales), META (+22% to $205B targeting ~14GW), and AMZN (+12% to $288B); all three projected negative FCF in 2027-28E. Morgan Stanley CIO survey pegs MSFT as the clearest public GenAI beneficiary. GS desk notes investors rotating into hyperscalers (GOOGL/MSFT/META/ORCL) vs. selling semis. Buffett's $10B GOOGL position signals conviction in AI capex ROIC thesis.

bullets.title: SHOP: Jefferies upgrades to Buy; agentic commerce seen as key long-term growth vector
bullets.body: Jefferies upgraded SHOP to Buy and hosted a feedback call at 2PM today. Investors received the upgrade constructively; catalysts include partner commission growth and potential price increases. Agentic commerce is seen as the structural LT vector but timing remains uncertain. Wedbush also transferred SHOP at Outperform with a $155 PT (25% upside from $123.55).

bullets.title: LITE: Citi opens 90-day upside catalyst watch; InP supply gap 30% in 2026, pricing +15% FY2027E
bullets.body: Citi initiated upside catalyst watch on LITE ahead of August 11 Q2 earnings and ECOC 2026. New InP model shows 30%/20%/11% demand-supply gap vs. supply for 2026-28E, supporting an additional 15% price increase in FY2027E and 6%/5% EPS upside revisions. LITE is shipping to NVIDIA today; CPO laser shipments expected to inflect Q4 2026. JPM also highlights LITE and COHR for DCI/OCS/CPO ramp in 2H26.

bullets.title: CSCO/ANET: Morgan Stanley VAR survey shows CSCO demand accelerating to +3.0%, ANET to +2.2%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's 2Q26 VAR survey upgraded CSCO growth expectations to 3.0% (from 0.6%) with 67% of VARs expecting sales increases; CSCO security sales expected to increase by 70% of VARs. ANET accelerated to 2.2% (from 1.0%) as the primary AI cluster and data center modernization beneficiary. AI/ML and security remain top IT spend priorities; AI additive not cannibalistic to networking budgets (54% net new funding).

bullets.title: RDDT: Jefferies positioned for 2Q upside; expects mid-single-digit revenue beat, stable DAU growth
bullets.body: Jefferies sees RDDT positioned for 2Q upside on strong ad checks, stable traffic, and sequential DAU growth. Investors are looking for revenue/EBITDA beats of mid-single-digit/low-double-digit vs. consensus. Wedbush initiates RDDT at Outperform with $250 PT (26% upside from $198).

bullets.title: ETSY: BTIG downgrades to Neutral from Buy on valuation at $85.74
bullets.body: BTIG cut ETSY to Neutral from Buy citing valuation concerns at $85.74. Stock was already trading down ~4.1% pre-market. Wedbush also transferred ETSY at Neutral with $80 PT, implying modest downside from current levels.

bullets.title: GLW: JPM places on negative catalyst watch ahead of Hardware/Networking earnings preview
bullets.body: JPMorgan placed GLW on negative catalyst watch, flagging weak TV display outlook as the primary risk; stock trades at 30x+ CY28E with the optical business alone at 40x+, leaving little room for error. JPM otherwise favors optical, EMS, and hardware subsectors into 2Q26 earnings.

bullets.title: UBER: Acquires Delivery Hero for $14.8B, expanding to 99 markets; also pledges €2B Germany investment
bullets.body: Uber offered €41.50/share ($14.8B equity value) for Delivery Hero; SSW Partners to acquire DHER's non-overlapping 14-market portfolio for $1.6B. Deal expected to close H2 2027. Uber also announced €2B Germany investment by 2031. Jefferies hosting a webinar on deal valuation, antitrust, and strategic implications.

bullets.title: AAPL: China AI approval granted; Apple Intelligence to launch with Alibaba/Baidu; exploring chip M&A
bullets.body: Beijing granted Apple license to roll out AI services on iPhone via CAC approval, with Alibaba and Baidu as technical partners. China is AAPL's second-largest market; iPhone sell-through tracking ~10% Y/Y YTD with recovery in C3Q. Separately, The Information reports Apple is seeking acquisitions of chip companies to boost server chip capabilities. AAPL hit a new all-time high, approaching $5T market cap.

bullets.title: MSFT: Coaching sales vs. Anthropic/OpenAI on cost/security; security exec overhaul underway
bullets.body: Microsoft is training its sales staff to pitch AI models as lower-cost alternatives to OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic, emphasizing cost advantages, security controls, and product completeness. Separately, new security chief Hayete Gallot is replacing at least 8 executives under former boss Charlie Bell to force an AI security overhaul, with several hundred additional cuts in the security group.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE: Strong server demand from CPU refresh and agentic workloads; supply-gated growth
bullets.body: JPM pre-quiet period check shows DELL sees structural multi-year server demand from CPU refresh and agentic workloads; storage demand materially stronger than reported (PowerScale/ObjectScale AI attach). HPE is supply-gated with DRAM as the primary constraint; server demand significantly outpacing storage. VAR channel confirms strong PC demand with teens unit growth in 3Q and workstation segment up ~20% YTD.

bullets.title: MSFT/NOW/SNOW: MS CIO survey—software fastest-growing at 4.1%; MSFT clearest GenAI beneficiary
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's 2Q26 CIO survey shows 2026 IT budget growth accelerating to 3.8% with software fastest-growing at 4.1% Y/Y. MSFT expected to grow 7.6% Y/Y (vs 6.3% in 2Q25), NOW 4.3%, SNOW 5.3%. Near-term budget revision ratio rose above 1.0x for the first time since 1Q24, signaling upside risk. Security screens as the cleanest category-level winner.

bullets.title: AMZN Q2 preview: AWS bogey ~31.5% Y/Y; OI guidance bogey ~$25B; Q3 AWS expected to accelerate further
bullets.body: JPM notes AWS revenue growth expected at ~31.5% Y/Y vs. a 35% buy-side bogey; operating income guidance of $20-24B vs. investor bogey of ~$25B is the key risk (concern over Prime Day expense shifts). Q3 2026 AWS expected to accelerate 2-3 more points. Buffett personally initiated Berkshire's $10B GOOGL position, signaling approval of AI data center ROIC thesis.

bullets.title: INTU: Citi cautious on FY27 estimate risk; QB Desktop decline and flat MC growth expected
bullets.body: Citi's off-quarter quiet period check on INTU flags near-term revenue trade-offs—QB Desktop decline and flat MC growth next year create a J-curve growth dynamic. RIF savings largely flow to the bottom line with mid-teens EPS growth achievable. Key debate centers on whether AI disruption risk is understated.

bullets.title: VRT: Baird initiates at Outperform with $370 PT on AI data center power demand
bullets.body: Baird initiated Vertiv (VRT) at Outperform with a $370 price target. VRT was pre-market trading down ~3.5% in sympathy with the broader semi/AI infrastructure selloff, which Baird views as a buying opportunity given the multi-year AI data center power buildout thesis.
